text:
Situation: As of 2026-10-21, dabigatran etexilate mesylate is not on the FDA drug shortage list. Current inventory across three sites provides limited coverage. Corvale East holds 13.3 days of 110 mg capsules and 32 days of 75 mg capsules. Corvale General holds 21.8 days and 26.5 days across two lots. Corvale Lakeside holds 20.3 days of 75 mg capsules.

Why (FDA record): The label for NDC 00597035556 lists Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG (FEI 3002806556) for API manufacture, labeling, manufacturing, and packing. FDA inspection 808119 of that plant ended 2012-11-12 and was classified OAI, with classification known to FDA on 2013-02-10. A Warning Letter was issued 2013-05-06. Subsequent inspections in 2014, 2016, 2018, 2021, and 2025 were classified VAI. The label also names Bidachem S.p.A. (FEI 3002806598) for analysis and API manufacture; its most recent inspection was classified VAI on 2024-05-17.

Our position: Supply is adequate for the near term but vulnerable given single-source API reliance and limited days on hand at Corvale East for the 110 mg strength. No FDA shortage listing exists to trigger allocation programs.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to qualify and purchase from A-S Medication Solutions to diversify 110 mg supply; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
2. Buyer to qualify and purchase from Alembic Pharmaceuticals Inc. for 75 mg and 110 mg strengths; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
3. Buyer to qualify and purchase from American Health Packaging for unit-dose packaging; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
4. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list weekly and report changes to P&T committee chair; requires buyer action only.

Not recommended: Switching patients to alternative anticoagulants or adjusting dosing regimens; those are clinical decisions for treating clinicians and the committee.
